text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lending rates at most Nigerian banks fall by two percent to 16 percent from last week, Daily Times investigations show.
- Federal government sets up 25-man committee to find solutions to the country's education crisis and map out strategy for the future.
- About 136 vehicles stolen in Nigeria have been traced to Cameroon, police inspector general Ibrahim Coomasie says.
- Government may have released more funds to joint venture oil partners to boost the vital oil sector, Guardian learnt.
- Appeal court defers ruling on issue of lawyer for detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola.
- Shell oil company takes over maintenance of hospital in volatile Ogoniland.
- Nigeria's crude oil output rises by two percent in first half of this year from preceeding six months, central bank report says.
- Nigeria calls off World Bank conference on investing in Nigeria due to begin in Washington on Friday because of U.S. refusal to give visas to Nigerian ministers.
- Two policemen, 23 others killed in riots on Wednesday in midwestern town of Auchi.
